subject: Why red
topic: Deep in the ocean, a surprising number of animals are bright red, like this shrimp.
script:
Deep in the ocean, a surprising number of animals are bright red, like this shrimp.
But red is actually one of the best colors for hiding down here.
Sunlight is made of many colors, and water soaks up red light first.
A few hundred meters down, the red light from the surface is basically gone.
With no red light to bounce off them, red animals look black, almost invisible.
So a red shrimp or a red jellyfish blends right into the darkness.
That's why so many deep-sea creatures wear red, from shrimp to jellies.
These red jellies were filmed almost a kilometer down, off the US West Coast.
Only when a robot shines its lights do their true colors appear.
Would you have guessed red is the color of invisibility?
